textbookBox.concept: Gundappa’s land has coconut trees planted in rows. Instead of counting the trees one by one, we count the number in one row and then count the rows.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Gundappa’s land has coconut trees planted in rows. Instead of counting the trees one by one, we count the number in one row and then count the rows.

beats.en: Muniamma arranges coconut laddoos and milk pedas in trays, and all the trays have the same arrangement. The trays are placed one above the other. We count what is in one tray and then multiply by the number of trays.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 maths · Pattern Around Us · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Shirley and Shiv arrange play money in neat patterns of notes and coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10 rupees.

beats.en: Shirley and Shiv arrange play money in neat patterns of notes and coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10 rupees. To count the money, we add the same coins together, count in tens first and then fives, twos and ones.
beats.speakEn: Shirley and Shiv arrange play money in neat patterns of notes and coins of 1, 2, 5 and 10 rupees. To count the money, we add the same coins together, count in tens first and then fives, twos and ones.

beats.en: Shirley and Shiv arrange coins in two different ways. Shiv puts them in pairs, two by two. Shirley’s arrangement always leaves one coin alone. So there is one extra.
beats.speakEn: Shirley and Shiv arrange coins in two different ways. Shiv puts them in pairs, two by two. Shirley’s arrangement always leaves one coin alone. So there is one extra.

textbookBox.concept: The even numbers up to 20 are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20. The odd numbers up to 20 are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19.
